summary: Polycam is a free phone scanner with a paid professional service around it, and in 2026 its centre of gravity has moved: the product describes itself first as a way of turning one phone scan into the documents a building job runs on — floor plans, as-builts, measurements, claim files — and second as a 3D capture tool. That reframing is the interesting part for this map, because it drags real-world units, measurement tolerance and computer-aided-design formats into a lane where almost nothing else has them. It captures with lidar, with photogrammetry, with Gaussian splats from photographs or video, with drone imagery and with 360 imagery, on iOS, Android, the web and Apple's headset. It exports more conventional formats than any other tool scored here — OBJ, DAE, FBX, STL, DXF, PLY and an insurance estimating format — and it will hand you a mesh derived from any splat, which is a bridge from captured content back to ordinary geometry that most of its peers do not offer. Against that, its splat interchange story is thin and it says so itself: support for splats in other software is a work in progress. Nothing it writes carries a licence, an author or a signature; there is no time axis anywhere; and the programmatic route out of the library — list captures, fetch metadata, export OBJ, glTF or LAS — is an enterprise add-on rather than part of the product everyone can use.

coverage.note: The application and the web viewer draw meshes, point clouds and splats well enough to edit and measure in. None of the pipeline is described or reachable from outside the product.

sources.quote: Polycam turns a single phone scan into the documents jobs run on: floor plans, as-builts, estimates, roof reports, claims files, measurements, and CAD-ready exports.

coverage.note: Polycam's Content Management API (bearer tokens scoped to one workspace) lists captures, updates capture metadata, exports and sends webhooks, and a separate limited-availability Reconstruction API takes uploaded photos and returns 3D models. It is an Enterprise add-on, changes are limited to metadata and exports, and the Reconstruction API is enabled by Polycam per workspace.

coverage.note: Polycam's developer-mode raw export gives one camera file per frame with intrinsics and a transform matrix, named by microsecond timestamp, so poses are time-ordered. The poses sit in an ARKit session frame and no interpolation rule is declared, and the export needs a LiDAR iOS device.

sources.title: Polycam polyform README (commit ad01118)
sources.quote: This directory contains the original images, where the name of the file is the timestamp in microseconds, and will match the filenames for the other corresponding files (camera, depth map etc).

sources.title: Polycam polyform README (commit ad01118)
sources.quote: This directory includes the `camera.json` files that hold the camera intrinsics and extrinsics, as well as the image `width`, `height` and a `blur_score` for the image

coverage.note: Polycam publishes a data specification for its raw export (per-frame images, camera files, depth maps and a mesh), but the specification names no extension scheme, version field or rule for readers that meet unknown fields. Searched the polyform README at commit ad01118 and the Polycam Content Management API page for extension, version, unknown and extra on 2026-10-20; found only application and processing version numbers in an API example and no extension rules. Polycam's app help pages were not searched.

coverage.note: Polycam offers a private or public setting on a capture, which is access control on its service rather than a protection scheme declared inside the content for recipients. Its purpose is mesh reconstruction, not protected-content delivery.
